questions.stem: Under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, which of these vessels is a pleasure craft?
options: A 9 m water taxi carrying paying passengers
A privately owned sailboat used only for pleasure that carries no passengers
A whale-watching boat run by a tour company
A fishing charter boat that takes paying guests
questions.explanation: The Act defines a pleasure craft as a vessel used for pleasure that does not carry passengers. Each of the other three carries passengers, so Part 4 applies to them even though they are small.

questions.stem: Who does the Act say is the master of a vessel?
options: The person in command and charge of the vessel
The most senior certificated person on board, whatever their role
The person who owns the vessel
Any licensed pilot on board while piloting
questions.explanation: The master is the person in command and charge. The owner may be on shore, and the definition specifically excludes a licensed pilot while the pilot performs pilotage duties.

questions.stem: A company owns a Canadian passenger vessel and has an arrangement with a Canadian operating corporation to be responsible for all matters not given to someone else by the Act. Who is the authorized representative?
options: The master, as the person in command
The owner, always
The Minister of Transport
The operating corporation, as a qualified person under the arrangement
questions.explanation: Section 14 makes the qualified person the authorized representative where the owner has made such an arrangement. The owner is the representative only in other cases, and the owner is bound by the representative's acts. The master has separate duties of their own.

questions.stem: Which list correctly gives the three general duties of an authorized representative in s. 106(1)?
options: Appoint the crew, set the hours of rest, inspect every voyage before departure
Hold the master's certificate, keep the log book, brief the passengers before each voyage
Obtain the documents before each voyage, keep the load lines clear, report hazards to the Minister
Ensure the vessel and equipment meet the regulations, develop procedures for safe operation and emergencies, ensure crew and passengers get safety training
questions.explanation: Section 106(1) lists those three duties. Obtaining documents before a voyage and keeping load lines clear are the master's duties (ss. 107 and 110). The other options mix duties that belong to nobody in that form.

questions.stem: When must a master ensure that all required Canadian maritime documents have been obtained?
options: At the start of each calendar year
Only when a marine safety inspector asks to see them
Before the vessel embarks on a voyage from a port in Canada
Within 30 days of the first voyage of the year
questions.explanation: Section 107 puts the check before departure from a Canadian port. It is a duty that arises with every voyage, not on request and not annually.

questions.stem: A vessel's certificate allows 12 persons. The master is clearing a harbour when 15 people from a capsized boat are picked up. May the master carry the extra people?
options: Yes, but only if the load lines are first marked on the hull
Yes, but only with the authorized representative's written approval
Yes, the person limit does not apply to shipwrecked or distressed persons carried because of the duty to rescue
No, the certificate limit can never be exceeded
questions.explanation: Section 110(3) says the limit in 110(1) does not apply to a person carried in pursuance of the obligation to carry shipwrecked or distressed persons. The master must still look after safety under s. 109, and the load-line rule in 110(2) still applies.

questions.stem: A deckhand notices a cracked fuel line fitting. What does the Act require the deckhand to do?
options: Wait until the next scheduled inspection
Report the safety hazard to the master
Report it to the Minister of Transport directly
Nothing, because only the master has duties on safety
questions.explanation: Section 113(b) requires every crew member to report any safety hazard they become aware of to the master. Crew have their own duties; they are not bystanders.

questions.stem: A master is told of a safety hazard on board that cannot be eliminated while the vessel is operating. What must the master of a Canadian vessel do besides taking reasonable measures to protect the vessel and people?
options: Stop the vessel and apply to the Minister for a direction
Notify the authorized representative
Record it in the log and take no other step
Ask the crew to sign a waiver
questions.explanation: Section 109(2) requires reasonable protective measures, including eliminating the hazard if feasible. If it is not feasible, the master of a Canadian vessel notifies the authorized representative.

questions.stem: Which of these is something every person, not just the crew, is forbidden to do under Part 4?
options: Operate a vessel without a master's certificate
Embark on a voyage without a chart
Carry a passenger without a lifejacket
Take any action that might jeopardize the safety of a vessel or the persons on board
questions.explanation: Section 118 prohibits any person from taking action that might jeopardize the safety of a vessel or persons on board. The other three are real requirements elsewhere (or different from what the option says) but are not the general prohibition in s. 118.

questions.stem: Part 4 (Safety) of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 applies to which vessels?
options: Only commercial vessels over 15 gross tonnage
All vessels of any flag, anywhere in the world
Canadian vessels everywhere other than pleasure craft, and foreign vessels in Canadian waters
Only vessels that hold an inspection certificate
questions.explanation: Section 105 sets that scope. It does not depend on size or on holding an inspection certificate, and it does not reach foreign vessels outside Canadian waters.

questions.stem: A passenger on a small BC tour boat is told by the skipper to move away from the bow rail during docking. What does the Act say about this?
options: The direction only binds the passenger if it is written on the safety card
The passenger may ignore it because only crew have duties
The passenger must comply with directions from the master or a crew member given to carry out the Act or the regulations
The passenger must comply only if the Minister has also given the direction
questions.explanation: Section 115(1) requires every passenger to comply with directions from the master or a crew member to carry out the Act or regulations. Section 115(2) separately requires compliance with a direction to leave the vessel before the voyage.
